Diagnose via the climate control head's self-test to identify the affected flap motor.
Test the bomb by counting assisted pedal strokes with the engine off (loss of assist in under ~10 strokes indicates a depleted accumulator).
Replace seals and pressure-test the system.
Test by listening: if the motor hums but produces no pressure/vacuum at the nipples, the internal graphite vanes have shattered.
If symptoms occur only with a specific phone, re-pair the device, update the phone OS, and test with wired versus wireless CarPlay/Android Auto.
Refill with the correct Audi-compatible coolant and bleed and re-pressure-test the system.
Test each sunroof drain separately with a modest amount of water, then clean a blocked hose with the proper sunroof-drain snake or the flexible cable method described in the repair manual.
The hose part number depends on body style, position, and VIN, so it must be selected from Audi's catalog after diagnosis.
If the belt has already jumped or broken, test compression and mechanical timing before buying a maintenance kit because cylinder-head repair may also be required.
otherwise continue diagnosing the plug, injector, wiring, compression, or another cause.
Six coils are installed, but replacing all six is optional maintenance, not the diagnostic conclusion.
Save DTCs and freeze-frame, then compare commanded and measured boost using the factory test conditions.
If the motor is silent, diagnose the fuse, switch, wiring, door control module, and motor.
Diagnose the vehicle according to the stored DTCs rather than ordering an ABS module from the warning alone.
persistent warnings still require diagnosis.

Persistent warm-engine rattle, rough running, no-start, or cam-crank correlation faults do not match this TSB and require a separate timing-system diagnosis before parts are ordered.
No owner-buyable part is published for this record until that diagnosis exists.
Audi specifies using air-suspension leak-detection tester VAS 751 001 to measure actual pressure and evaluate compressor output.
A real sag, leak, run-time, or ride-height complaint still requires the separate factory leak, valve-block, air-spring, relay, wiring, temperature-protection, and compressor diagnostics for that VIN.
This bulletin itself specifies a diagnostic tool rather than a replacement part, so the old product links are removed.
For a warning outside an open campaign, use Audi ODIS-guided diagnosis and preserve the complete code, symptom number, and actual mode.
Audi must select the correct starter-alternator suffix and associated hardware by VIN and guided-test result.
Do not buy a scanner, repair manual, or replacement gateway module as the recall fix.
a module already affected by liquid requires vehicle-specific diagnosis and campaign or warranty handling.
Other black-screen, reboot, camera, connectivity, or control faults require their own diagnosis rather than automatic display replacement.
It is not the auxiliary HVAC pump and is not a diagnosis for every coolant warning.

Diagnose by starting the engine cold so the SAI system runs and listening for the vacuum leak, then looking around for the crack.

Replace brittle vacuum hose with silicone, test combi valves with a hand vacuum pump (they should hold vacuum and audibly click open), and if codes persist with new vacuum/valves the SAI ports in the head will need to be carbon-cleaned.
The recall remedy involves an onboard diagnostic software update that monitors battery modules in real-time for anomalies and can isolate affected modules.
if symptoms persist, diagnose and replace the clutch pack or mechatronic unit as required.

In some cases, the sunroof cassette requires re-indexing via scan tool.
If software does not resolve, diagnosis will determine if the 48V battery, BSG, or DC-DC converter needs replacement.
perform a consumption test if usage exceeds Audi's threshold.
Perform a leak-down test BEFORE walnut blasting to ensure intake valves seat properly.
Diagnose the misfiring cylinder(s) via the stored misfire counters, then replace the failed coil(s) along with spark plugs;
Fresh, correct-spec hydraulic fluid and a proper bleed with a diagnostic tool are required.

Diagnose the lift pump/hydraulic circuit;

Diagnose the concern by scanning for boost-control and turbocharger actuator faults, logging requested vs.
Diagnose with live fuel-rail pressure data before condemning the pump, as a faulty low-pressure sensor or in-tank pump can set the same codes.

Diagnose whether the fault is the gas struts (won't stay up / weak lift), the spindle lift motors (slow or struggling travel), or the latch/cinching motor (won't release or won't pull closed — see TSB 2072431/1).
For judder/jerking, have the mechatronic unit tested;
Test/replace the shark-fin antenna module with a matching OEM part number and renew the base gasket to restore a watertight seal;
Test the drains by slowly pouring water into the channels at each corner of the sunroof and watching where it exits beneath the A- and C-pillars.
Diagnose per TSB 2046724 with a fuel-pressure decay test to isolate a leaking HPFP versus leaking injectors.
Clear codes and re-test crankcase pressure after the repair.
